title.value: Sociotechnical Harms of Algorithmic Systems: Scoping a Taxonomy for Harm Reduction
title.justification: The title explicitly states the focus on assessing harms that arise from algorithmic systems and offers a taxonomy for reducing these harms.
title.quote: Sociotechnical Harms of Algorithmic Systems: Scoping a Taxonomy for Harm Reduction

extractions.description: This paper presents a scoping review of sociotechnical harms from algorithmic systems, offering a taxonomy to help practitioners and researchers systematically identify and address harms across five major themes: representational, allocative, quality-of-service, interpersonal, and societal. It emphasizes how the interplay of technical and social dynamics can reinforce unjust hierarchies and offers a framework for systematic harm anticipation and reduction.

primary_category.justification: The focus of the paper is on understanding and categorizing the harms of algorithmic systems for harm reduction, which does not specifically align with any eco-responsible categories like climate change or pollution.
primary_category.quote: Harms from algorithmic systems encompass both computational and contextual harms, focusing on social and ethical dimensions.

secondary_categories.justification: The primary aim is categorizing and understanding algorithmic harms, which doesn't directly intersect with established eco-responsible AI categories.
secondary_categories.quote: ...this taxonomy navigates the challenging task of synthesizing multidisciplinary computing research with different priorities and concerns.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category for eco-responsible AI doesn't apply here since the taxonomy focuses on social and ethical harms of algorithmic systems.
primary_sub_category.quote: This taxonomy of sociotechnical harms offers a systematic view of types of harms from algorithmic systems but does not focus on environmental or resource-based impacts.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As the paper primarily discusses sociotechnical harms, no eco-responsible sub-categories overlap with its main focus.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We recognize the complex and often concurrent ways harms are experienced within sociotechnical systems.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper provides a structured approach to understanding and mitigating harms arising from algorithmic systems, centralizing the reduction of sociotechnical harms in its methodology and taxonomy.
new_primary_category.quote: The final taxonomy builds on and refers to existing taxonomies, classifications, and terminologies for harm reduction in algorithmic systems.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper develops a taxonomy to systematically understand and address harms related to the interaction of algorithmic systems and social dynamics.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We present an applied taxonomy of sociotechnical harms to support a more systematic surfacing of potential harms in algorithmic systems.
